measures.name: Initiative Measure IP26-645
measures.summary: Official ballot title: Initiative Measure No. IP26-645 concerns state and local taxes. This measure would repeal a 9.9% tax on annual individual income over $1,000,000; prohibit taxes measured by individual income and taxes on individual income or the receipt of individual income; and define “income.” This measure would decrease funding for public K-12 education, higher education (including universities and community colleges), and human services (primarily healthcare). Should this measure be enacted into law?

measures.name: Initiative Measure IL26-001
measures.summary: Repeals amendments to the statute listing rights of parents and guardians of public-school children and re-enacts the law as originally enacted by Initiative to the Legislature 2081 (per the pamphlet summary page).

measures.name: Initiative Measure IL26-638
measures.summary: Official ballot title: concerns participation in athletics at K-12 schools. Would prohibit students it defines as "biologically male" from competing in certain school athletic activities intended for female students only, and would require verification of biological sex by students' healthcare providers.

measures.name: Pierce County Charter Amendment No. 52 (County Council meetings)
measures.summary: Charter Review Commission proposal (Approved/Rejected): requires the County Council to meet at least 45 times each year and requires Council meetings that take public comment to offer remote attendance and public comment. Per official sample-ballot text.

measures.name: Pierce County Charter Amendment No. 53 (Appointed Sheriff and Termination of Elected Sheriff)
measures.summary: Charter Review Commission proposal (Approved/Rejected): would make the Sheriff an appointed (by the Executive, confirmed by a majority of the County Council) rather than elected office, ending the current elected term early, effective January 1, 2027. Per official sample-ballot text.

measures.name: Pierce County Charter Amendment No. 54 (Public Safety Ombuds)
measures.summary: Charter Review Commission proposal (Approved/Rejected): creates an executive department of Public Safety Ombuds to provide independent oversight of the Sheriff and Sheriff's Office employees. Per official sample-ballot text.

measures.name: Pierce County Charter Amendment No. 55 (Initiative Procedures)
measures.summary: Charter Review Commission proposal (Approved/Rejected): gives initiative sponsors 180 days to collect signatures in support of a proposed initiative. Per official sample-ballot text.

measures.name: Pierce County Charter Amendment No. 56 (Four Year Budget Outlook)
measures.summary: Charter Review Commission proposal (Approved/Rejected): requires the Chief Financial Officer to prepare a four-year budget outlook for the next and succeeding biennial budgets, establishing that projected expenditures will not exceed projected available funds. Per official sample-ballot text.

measures.name: Pierce County Charter Amendment No. 57 (Nondiscrimination)
measures.summary: Charter Review Commission proposal (Approved/Rejected): revises the prohibition on discrimination in the performance of County duties so that it may not infringe on, diminish, or impair any right secured by the U.S. or Washington State Constitution. Per official sample-ballot text.

measures.name: Pierce County Charter Amendment No. 58 (Juvenile Detention)
measures.summary: Charter Review Commission proposal (Approved/Rejected): creates a Juvenile Detention Advocate Office to respond to complaints, monitor conditions and comply with regulations, and subjects Juvenile Detention to an independent audit or accreditation review at least once every five years. Per official sample-ballot text.

measures.name: Pierce Transit Proposition No. 1 (Maintaining and Expanding Local Transit Service Sales and Use Tax Increase)
measures.summary: Would authorize an additional sales and use tax of three-tenths of one percent to maintain and improve transit service (more routes and event service, longer service hours, shorter waits, access to light rail, healthcare, schools and jobs, expanded service for people with disabilities, fare-free service for seniors and youth), effective April 1, 2027. Approved/Rejected.

measures.name: City of Tacoma Initiative Measure No. 1 (Safe Homes for All)
measures.summary: Concerns tenant safety and protection laws: landlord education and training, recognizing tenants' right to organize, requiring landlords to bargain in good faith with tenant unions, a public landlord information database, City and private enforcement with penalties and cost recovery, landlord rental licensing and fees, license revocation, anti-retaliation, and certain exemptions. Yes/No.

unverified: Pierce County Council district for the Municipal Building: a county Charter Review Commission page snippet (page returned 403 to automated access, seen only as a search snippet) and the Wikipedia council table both place downtown Tacoma in District 4. The official sample ballot lists County Council Districts 1, 5 and 7 only, so no council race is shown for this address; this rests on District 4 not being up in 2026 and is UNVERIFIED by the county's own GIS Council District Locator.

Congressional (6) and legislative (27) districts: from the U.S. Census Bureau geocoder run on the address, consistent with the sample ballot's LD 27 and CD 6 sections; not checked against the VoteWA address lookup.

How the ballot was matched to the address: the official Pierce County sample ballot is county-wide, so only contests that apply to the address are kept (CD 6; LD 27; county-wide offices; Supreme Court; Court of Appeals Div. 2 Dist. 1; county-wide District Court Positions 1-8; state and county charter measures; Pierce Transit Prop. 1, whose area includes Tacoma; City of Tacoma Initiative 1; Tacoma Municipal Court). Other Pierce County contests (other congressional and legislative districts, council districts, the Southeast Electoral District judge positions, and Milton, South Prairie, Fire District 14, Yelm and Auburn measures) do not apply to a Tacoma address.

Sample-ballot text was read from a text extraction of the county PDF; for District Court Position 7, the extraction lists two names (Pam Nogueira, Mike Sommerfeld) without a separate position label, so the pairing is read from layout.

Not researched: Pierce County Auditor, Court races, Tacoma and county measures other than IP26-645. No candidate withdrawals appear on the sample ballot. Mitch Townsend, listed earlier, is a Lewis County Auditor candidate (PDC), not a Pierce County candidate.
Party labels shown are as printed on the sample ballot (for example 'Prefers Democratic Party').

In her voters' pamphlet statement she lists a balanced budget each year and no income tax among her priorities.
In her voters' pamphlet statement she lists prioritizing public safety, supporting law enforcement and stopping drug trafficking among her priorities.
In her voters' pamphlet statement she lists voter identification and electing the county Sheriff among her priorities.

races.race: Initiative Measure IP26-645 (taxes on individual income)
races.summary: IP26-645 would repeal the 9.9% tax on annual individual income over $1,000,000 enacted in 2026 and prohibit state and local taxes on individual income.
races.turns_on: Whether the revenue the tax would raise is worth more to you than the measure's broader ban on income taxes, given the state's $11.4 billion revenue-loss estimate over fiscal years 2027-2031.
races.yes_means: A yes vote repeals the 9.9% tax on individual income over $1,000,000 before it begins in 2028 and prohibits taxes measured by individual income (Attorney General explanatory statement, https://www.sos.wa.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/Voters%20Pamphlet%202026%20-%20Edition%2009%20-%20Pierce.pdf).
races.no_means: A no vote leaves the 2026 law (ESSB 6346) in place, so the 9.9% tax on individual income over $1,000,000 begins in calendar year 2028 (Attorney General explanatory statement, https://www.sos.wa.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/Voters%20Pamphlet%202026%20-%20Edition%2009%20-%20Pierce.pdf).
races.fiscal: The Office of Financial Management estimates a state revenue loss of $11,432,414,000 over fiscal years 2027-2031, mainly from the general fund, with no impact on local revenue (https://www.sos.wa.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/Voters%20Pamphlet%202026%20-%20Edition%2009%20-%20Pierce.pdf).

for.text: Argument for, written by Chris Gildon and others: Washingtonians have rejected an income tax ten times, and the measure 'restores your right to decide'.

against.text: Argument against, written by the Washington Education Association, Washington State Labor Council and others: the measure cuts billions for education and healthcare and benefits those earning over $1 million.

evidence.text: Official ballot title (voters' pamphlet): "Initiative Measure No. IP26-645 concerns state and local taxes. This measure would repeal a 9.9% tax on annual individual income over $1,000,000; prohibit taxes measured by individual income and taxes on individual income or the receipt of individual income; and define “income.” This measure would decrease funding for public K-12 education, higher education (including universities and community colleges), and human services (primarily healthcare). Should this measure be enacted into law?"

Office of Financial Management fiscal impact statement: estimated state revenue loss of $11,432,414,000 over state fiscal years 2027-2031; $3.108 billion in FY2029, $4.432 billion in FY2030, $3.892 billion in FY2031.

PDC (state open-data set, queried 2026-10-16): Vote Yes Repeal the Income Tax reports $1,989,245.00 in contributions and $1,579,072.00 in expenditures; Let's Go Washington (Sponsored by Brian Heywood), registered for IL26-001, IL26-638 and IL26-645, reports $3,908,180.50 in contributions and $3,917,168.54 in expenditures across all three measures.

PDC (state open-data set, queried 2026-10-16): No on 645 reports $12,269,814.62 in contributions and $7,354,424.83 in expenditures; Millionaire's Tax Washington (against) reports $243,799.00 in contributions and $219,039.23 in expenditures.

The pamphlet printed an argument for (Gildon and others) and an argument against (Washington Education Association, Washington State Labor Council and others), each with a rebuttal; the argument against names one YES-side funder.

gaps: Prosecutor race: no voted or decided records found for either candidate from sources I could open; both candidates' items are campaign-site statements and PDC totals. No League of Women Voters or Vote411 questionnaire was found.
Teresa Fox and Carole Sue Braaten have no legislative record; Braaten has no PDC totals.
Measure funding is committee-level; top donors were not listed.

Official county sample ballot was read from an extracted-text copy of the PDF; the county Elections site and council-district pages returned 403 to automated access, so local measures other than the listing were not researched (only IP26-645 was, so 4 items).

FEC: Randall's figures run through 2026-09-30; the FEC page for Teresa Fox still showed the 2026-07-15 report when checked 2026-10-16 (newly filed data can lag up to 48 hours), so her row is unchanged.

PDC figures are from the state open-data campaign summary queried 2026-10-16; no Oct 6-16 debates, forums, rulings, bar ratings or new endorsements were found from sources opened for the researched items (the Supreme Court 4-4 ruling on the IP26-645 fiscal-statement wording and the Steves/Jennings endorsements predate Oct 6).
